A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PurpCode study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v3 reports original safety, overrefusal, utility, training-stage, and sampling experiments, plus analyzer comparisons and case studies in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports validation of its malicious-assistance judge in Section 2.1.

M1.justification: The rule-learning/SFT stage, GRPO reinforcement learning, reward structure, single-step dynamic sampling, batched reward calculation, and red-teaming procedures remain unchanged. Added judge validation and expanded oracle descriptions do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Training corpora, benchmark tasks, programming-language coverage, and single- and multi-turn evaluation scenarios are retained. The new judge validation uses the existing CyberSecEval MITRE benchmark rather than extending task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Section 2.1 adds Sonnet 4 and DeepSeek-R1 as alternative judges alongside Llama-3.3-70B in an agreement check, with human annotations as a reference. The frontier-model, SafeCoder/ProSec, dynamic-sampler, and static-analyzer comparison sets otherwise remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v4 introduces cross-model judge agreement and comparison with human annotations as an additional validation procedure, although its sampling and aggregation details are unspecified. Existing decoding settings, token budgets, benchmark construction, and 14B/32B experimental settings are retained after relocation.

E4.justification: v4 adds the judge-robustness check in Section 2.1 but removes v3 Section 4.5's brief preliminary finding that RL without rule learning was ineffective. The detailed training-stage, sampler, analyzer, and reasoning/jailbreak analyses remain, mostly in relocated appendices.

E5.justification: Both versions report greedy decoding by default and averages of three runs for o4-mini. v4's checklist acknowledges the absence of error bars but adds no uncertainty estimates, significance tests, or changed run counts. The new judge-agreement percentage is a result, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v4 newly reports 94.5% judge consistency on CyberSecEval MITRE and less than 2% difference from human annotations. It replaces the CodeQL 'CWE-XXX' entry with 'CWE-20*' at the same frequency of 8 in Table 14, formerly Table 13. Benchmark scores remain identical; the preliminary RL-only failure and zero-flag decontamination findings are omitted.

T1.justification: The GRPO advantage expression and dynamic-sampling calculation are retained. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs, and v4 adds no substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, or derivations.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims of a first open-source cybersafety reasoning alignment recipe, strong safety relative to frontier models, reduced overrefusal, and preserved utility. The shortened introduction and edited conclusion do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix B expands the discussion of benchmark insufficiency and proposes harder multi-turn and broader-CWE evaluations, plus dynamic or ensemble analysis oracles. Single-turn-only RL was already acknowledged in v3. v4 also removes the explanation linking the preliminary RL-only failure to inadequate safety-reasoning trajectories.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly documents H100/H200 GPU configurations, memory, workload allocation, API providers, and asset licensing. Resource links remain unchanged, while the explicit StarCoder2 decontamination-configuration statement is shortened. Licensing disclosures conflict internally: the checklist says all artifacts are research-only, whereas Appendix C specifies Apache-2.0 source code.

R1.justification: Research positioning in Section 5 remains stable. Limited source substitutions include replacing the SandboxFusion repository reference with FullStack Bench and the Claude 3.5 Haiku product reference with a model-card addendum. Most other bibliography changes update publication metadata or consolidate H4RM3L references.

P1.justification: v4 substantially reorganizes the document: jailbreak details move from Section 3.3 to Appendix D.1, controlled experiments from Section 4.5 to Appendix E.2, and sampling/XSCode details to Appendix E.1. It also adds a conference checklist and limitations/resources sections, restructures the remaining appendices, and edits substantial portions of the main narrative.

P2.justification: v4 adds a license table, relocates experimental tables, compacts the CWE-frequency table beside its discussion, and gives three existing case-study examples numbered Figure 5–7 captions. These are localized display and placement revisions; the principal diagrams, plots, and experimental table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added judge validation and hardware details improve evidential support and reproducibility, but the validation lacks sample-size and annotation-protocol details. v4 also removes the preliminary RL-only negative finding and introduces checklist contradictions, including denying LLM use despite the paper's methods and conflicting licensing statements. These benefits and reporting regressions prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
